Shri Anil Khare - Senior Advocate assisted by Shri Pr  - Advocate for the applicant.
Shri Aditya Gupta - Panel Lawyer for the State.
Shri Manoj Kumar Rajak - Advocate for the complainant

ORDER This is first application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.762/2023 registered at Police Station - Sihora, District - Jabalpur for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 376 (2) (n) and 506 of the Indian Penal Code.
He is in custody since 13.03.2026.
2. Learned senior counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated.
The applicant has already divorced from his earlier marriage as per triable customs as he belongs to the scheduled tribe.
It is further contended that the applicant and the complainant have entered into wedlock and their marriage certificate has also been filed along with this application.

As per FIR their relationship began in NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:24070 2 MCRC-13171-2026 the year 2021 and continued up to 2023 and they have consumed life as husband and wife on several occasions.
The complainant is a 33 years old lady having knowledge and understanding of consequences of such relationship.
She willing entered into such relationship with the petitioner and such relationship continued for about more than two years as per FIR itself.
It is also stated that the complainant has herself filed an affidavit in support of this application for grant of bail.
The applicant is a Station House Officer and he is not having any criminal antecedent and also he will be available for the proceeding of trial, if discretion is exercised in his favour.

He has drawn attention of this Court to the affidavit and marriage certificate and contended that considering the totality of facts and circumstances of the case, in the peculiar facts of the case, no offence is made out.

The trial will take considerable time and, therefore, it is prayed that Girish Dhurve vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 24 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163625277/
1 the applicant be released on bail.

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the complainant submits at the Bar that the complainant is present in Court.
It is submitted that the complainant has got married with the present applicant and she has no objection if bail is granted to the applicant.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer by saying that there are serious allegations levelled against the present applicant who is a police officer.
It is further contended that offences were registered on 28.10.2023 but the applicant could be arrested only on 13.03.2026.
Therefore, it is prayed that his application may be dismissed.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:24070 3 MCRC-13171-2026 5.
I have considered the rival submission made at the Bar and perused the case diary.
Though the complainant is present in Court yet this Court does not deem it fit to verify the contents of the affidavit filed by her.
However, counsel for the State has verified the Aadhar Card of the complainant and her identity and also verified the fact that the affidavit has been filed by her.

So far as consent of the complainant is concerned, looking to the seriousness of allegations and in view of the judgments of the Apex Court, it should not be considered in the larger interest of the society.
However, in the present case, both the applicant and the complainant are major.

From the material available on record, it transpires that the applicant had already got divorce from his earlier marriage as per customary tradition prevalent in his community as he belongs to the scheduled tribe.
After registration of the FIR, the applicant and the complainant got married and marriage certificate is also filed along with the application.

They are in relationship as husband and wife for a long time i.e.
about two years.

Therefore, considering the peculiar facts of the case coupled with the fact that trial will take a considerable time, without expressing any view on the merits of the case, I deem it a fit case to release the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the application is allowed.

6. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:24070 4 MCRC-13171-2026 he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of BNSS, 2023.
He will not indulge in any such activity which affects the process of investigation process of trial in any manner.
He will not try to influence any of the witnesses during the course of trial.
7. This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
